title: The physics floor
summary: How far a multiply-add, an AI word or a photo is from the energy floor physics sets, why cooling cannot beat it, and how far a signal can go in one tick.

born: Rolf Landauer shows that erasing one bit of information must turn at least kT ln 2 of energy into heat.
then: The floor is pure theory: computers are built from separate transistors and the first chips, far above any physical limit.
Charles Bennett shows that computing without erasing, reversibly, could in principle go below that floor.
Experiments measure the heat of erasing a single bit and find it close to Landauer's limit.
Chips still spend millions of times the floor on each operation, most of it moving data rather than computing.

learn.plain: Every time a computer forgets a bit, a tiny amount of energy must turn into heat: physics sets that minimum, like a toll on every erased bit. Today's chips pay millions of times the toll on each step, mostly to move numbers between memory and the place where the math happens, the way a cook spends more effort walking to the fridge than chopping. Cooling the chip lowers the toll but costs just as much to pump the heat away, and nothing can cross the chip faster than light.
learn.engineer: Landauer: erasing a bit dissipates at least kT ln 2 (2.87 zJ at 300 K). A b-bit array multiply-add erases on the order of b² bits, so the floor for a 16-bit MAC is about 1 aJ, while a 45 nm chip spends about 0.8 pJ on the arithmetic and 0.24 pJ to 1.3 nJ fetching operands from registers, SRAM or DRAM (Horowitz numbers as tabulated by Dally et al.). Reuse (batching, tiling) and locality cut the movement term; precision cuts both terms and the floor. Cooling to T lowers the device floor by T/300 but the Carnot work to reject the heat at 300 K exactly restores it, so cryogenic logic never wins on thermodynamic energy alone. The speed floor is the propagation speed c/√εr (about 0.5c in SiO2); real RC wires are far slower. The model leaves out leakage, clocking, control overhead, and newer processes, which shift every bar down by a few times without closing the gap.

quiz.q: What sets the minimum energy to erase one bit?
quiz.why: Landauer's limit is kT ln 2: Boltzmann's constant times the temperature times ln 2. No device detail appears in it.

quiz.q: For one AI word at batch size 1, where does most of the energy go?
options: Erasing bits at the Landauer limit
quiz.why: Every weight is read from DRAM once per word, and a DRAM read costs thousands of times a multiplication.

quiz.q: A perfect refrigerator cools a chip to 4 K. What happens to the energy per erased bit, counting the refrigerator?
options: It stays exactly the same as at room temperature
quiz.why: The chip's floor falls by 300/4, and the ideal refrigerator spends exactly that saving to pump the heat back to 300 K.
